repair_actions: Bind the canonical repository identity outside the artifact: the remote URL, host and repository slug must come from a constant that the resolver does not read from a caller-writable file, and acceptance of an artifact HEAD should additionally require a verifiable signature or an out-of-band published-revision attestation rather than reachability on whatever remote the local policy names.

Byte-verify every load-bearing local artifact the validator enforces, not only the resolver module and the trust policy: at minimum lf_common_evidence_envelope_v0_5_candidate.schema.json, lf_shared_authority_typed_context_v0_2_candidate.schema.json and validate_s38_dg_contracts_v0_5.py, using the same _verify_local_against_canonical path executed before first use.

Re-verify or immutably snapshot the trust policy at the point of use for claim-tier ceiling, witness allowlist and archival registry decisions, so that these three controls do not inherit a single unanchored root.

Neutralise caller transport environment for the canonical fetch (https_proxy, HTTPS_PROXY, ALL_PROXY, GIT_PROXY_COMMAND, GIT_SSL_NO_VERIFY, GIT_SSL_CAINFO, SSL_CERT_FILE) in _canonical_remote_env, and stop mapping fetch-transport failures to BLOCK_GOVERNED_ARTIFACT_HEAD_UNPUBLISHED, which misreports a network condition as a publication verdict.

Extend the bundle pin model to express historical refs so the archival currentness fixture at be6c0f8a320c5cdcfa242ee775ba769745eb82df is pinned as exercised evidence rather than only digest-bound inside the policy.

Add the eight mandatory attacks absent from the producer harness (unpublished canonical revision, unregistered archival identity, owner capability mismatch, authority and provenance replay without common binding, the three same-content identity substitutions, governed-input mismatch, weakened forbidden-authority set) so the deterministic suite covers the declared attack surface.
remaining_risks: Trust-anchor circularity: an adversary who controls the checkout the validation stack runs from can redirect canonical_repository.remote_url, publish the altered policy to their own remote and obtain verified=True with forged evidence bytes served under the genuine repository slug and the claim ceiling raised to BEHAVIORAL. Executed and reproduced in this review.

Enforced-surface tampering: mutating only the v0.5 evidence schema in the local checkout, with resolver module and policy untouched and artifact HEAD published, admits undeclared envelope surface with a full PASS at PROVENANCE_EXECUTION. Executed and reproduced in this review.

Claim-tier and archival-currentness controls are correct against their declared attacks but derive their entire authority from the same unanchored trust policy, so both fall with the first risk rather than independently.

Canonical fetch remains sensitive to caller transport environment; observed effect here was denial only, and TLS-intercepting byte substitution was not executed, so the exploitability of that path is unresolved rather than excluded.

The empty witness allowlist makes SEMANTIC and BEHAVIORAL structurally unreachable today; the witness path itself is therefore untested against a real allowlisted provider and must be re-reviewed when the first entry is added.
One load-bearing artifact exercised by this review is not covered by the 43 frozen pins.
